artifacts.summary: Recommends treating an off-vocabulary .orchestrator-handoff.json status as equivalent to a missing handoff (permit, deferring to artifact evidence) with a mandatory loud diagnostic naming the offending value and the six legal values, while continuing to refuse on-vocabulary non-matching statuses unchanged; also identifies the partial branch's inline duplicate check (lines 433-442) as a second call site needing the same consolidation.

memory_candidates.content: In agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/reconcile-task-status.sh, an off-vocabulary (malformed) .orchestrator-handoff.json status value should be treated as equivalent to a MISSING handoff (permit promotion, deferring to artifact-on-disk evidence) rather than refused, because it carries strictly less information than a genuine on-vocabulary refusal signal (blocked/partial/failed). The file's own artifact_newer_than_last_update() already names this governing principle explicitly: 'signal absent -> permit' philosophy. Refusing on malformed status (the pre-fix behavior) treats malformed as worse than absent, which is backwards and produces a genuine unrecoverable wedge since record_refused_promotion() only records blocked|partial and no-ops on anything else, including malformed values.

orchestrate-recover-outcome.sh is a separate, deliberately narrow .return-meta.json-consultation mechanism used only by skill-orchestrate Stage 5 / Stage MT-4 when a handoff is missing or STALE -- never for a malformed-but-present handoff, and never as a generic fallback. Its own 'Item C decision' comment explicitly rejects adding permissive off-schema fallbacks, to keep writer drift visible. Do not route a malformed-handoff fix for reconcile-task-status.sh (or similar scripts) through this mechanism -- it belongs to a different call site with a different, deliberately stricter philosophy.
